solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person enlisted to study handwriting (9)

blocks.note: to con is to study or pore over

annotation.surface: A new recruit is sent off to learn graphology.
annotation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old-fashioned verb (to con a lesson) that setters use constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: A conscript is a person compulsorily enlisted into the armed forces.

clue.text: Opportunity to go over large part of church (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over (above) the next

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: Someone gets a chance to go over a big section of a church, perhaps on a tour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go over' reads as inspect or revisit; in a down clue it just means CHANCE is written above L.
annotation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, where clergy and choir sit.

clue.text: Observing deficiency in action of bell? (6)

blocks.note: a ting is the sound a small bell makes

annotation.surface: Someone notices that a bell is not ringing properly.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'action of bell' is a playful way of describing its ring, TING.
annotation.definitionFit: Noting and observing both mean noticing or remarking on something.

clue.text: Dubious activity of primate disturbing current king (5)

indicators.note: APE gets in between C and R, breaking them up

blocks.note: C = current, the abbreviation used in electrical notation such as AC and DC

annotation.surface: A monkey up to no good upsets the reigning monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current king' reads as the monarch now on the throne; it is two separate abbreviations, C and R.
annotation.definitionFit: A caper is an escapade, often a slightly illegal one such as a heist.

clue.text: Conditions originally ideal for skiing (3)

indicators.note: take each word at its origin: the first letter

blocks.note: the first letters of Ideal For Skiing

annotation.surface: Weather and snow were perfect for a day on the slopes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conditions' in the surface means snow conditions; as the definition it means provisos, as in 'no ifs or buts'.
annotation.definitionFit: Ifs are conditions or provisos attached to something.

clue.text: Meticulous cabbie’s passenger in public highway (12)

blocks.note: a taxi driver calls a passenger a fare

annotation.surface: A careful taxi driver's customer is being carried along a main road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads the apostrophe-s as possession; it is the passenger, the FARE, who is the second piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a road open to the public, usually a main one.

clue.text: Fruit, penny apiece (5)

annotation.surface: A market price label: fruit at a penny each.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a price tag, so 'penny apiece' reads as one idea; it splits into P and EACH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the peach is one particular fruit, the stone fruit with downy skin.

clue.text: Miserly minister snatching this writer’s promissory notes (12)

indicators.note: PARSON grabs I'M and holds it inside

blocks.note: a parson is a minister of the church
this writer is = I am = I'M
IOUs are notes promising to pay

annotation.surface: A stingy clergyman takes the author's IOUs off them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is the setter speaking of themselves: I'M, with the 's standing for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Parsimonious means extremely unwilling to spend money, miserly.

clue.text: Endlessly recommend imbibing a liqueur (8)

indicators.note: ADVOCAT drinks in the A, holding it inside

annotation.surface: Someone keeps recommending that you drink a particular liqueur.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' before liqueur looks like part of the definition but is the letter taken inside. Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur.
annotation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a thick yellow Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy.

clue.text: A new piece of advice in respect of hors d’oeuvre (9)

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice

annotation.surface: Someone offers a fresh suggestion about starters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In respect of' reads as a connecting phrase but is the final piece, AS TO.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian name for an hors d'oeuvre, the starter before the main course.

clue.text: Hastened to protect extremely vulnerable bird (5)

indicators.note: RAN goes round the letters, shielding them
take the extremes, first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone rushed over to shield a defenceless bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely vulnerable' reads as very defenceless; it asks for the extremes of 'vulnerable', V and E.
annotation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Singer left in badly torn coat (9)

indicators.note: the letters of TORN COAT are rearranged
L goes inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A singer was left wearing a badly ripped coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned; it is just L, slipped into the jumbled coat.
annotation.definitionFit: A contralto is a singer with the lowest female voice.

clue.text: Having free time, idles casually round Yorkshire river (8)

indicators.note: the letters of IDLES are arranged any old how
the rearranged IDLES goes round URE

blocks.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

annotation.surface: Someone with time on their hands lounges about by a river in Yorkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a county in northern England, and a crossword favourite for its three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Leisured means having plenty of free time, as in the leisured classes.

clue.text: Miserable male, one leaving without difficulty (6)

annotation.surface: A gloomy man walks out without any fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Miserable' here means paltry, not unhappy: a measly sum is a miserable one.
annotation.definitionFit: Measly means contemptibly small or poor, like a miserable amount.

clue.text: Tedious procedure for making hole (6)

blocks.note: the noun for drilling, as a drill does into wood or rock

annotation.surface: Drilling holes is a dull job.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one complaint, but it is two meanings of the same word side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Boring means both dull and the act of drilling a hole.

clue.text: Figure of old Charlie — with label attached (7)

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A picture of old Charlie, complete with a name tag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a portrait or a person's shape; it is a geometric figure.
annotation.definitionFit: An octagon is a plane figure with eight sides.

clue.text: Excellent environment for the Spanish cat (6)

indicators.note: FINE surrounds EL, as an environment surrounds what lives in it

annotation.surface: A great home for a Spanish cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' is the Spanish word for 'the', EL.
annotation.definitionFit: A feline is a cat, or any member of the cat family.

clue.text: It nourishes teachers introducing old verse books (9)

indicators.note: NUT comes first, leading in the other pieces

blocks.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teachers' union
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in the Rime of the Ancient Mariner
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Teachers bring in poetry books that feed the mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The NUT was the British National Union of Teachers. 'Books' is the New Testament, NT.
annotation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishing food, the thing that nourishes.

clue.text: Drive in Mercedes passing elegant Lotus first of all (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of all the words before it

blocks.note: the first letters of In Mercedes Passing Elegant Lotus

annotation.surface: A motorist in a Mercedes overtakes a stylish Lotus sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive' in a clue full of cars reads as motoring; it is the verb to force forward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to impel something is to push or force it forward, as a motor drives a car.

clue.text: A brief hearing in the courts once (5)

indicators.note: TRIAL is cut short, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A short legal hearing in the courts of the past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Courts' in a legal surface means law courts; here it means courtyards, the open halls of Roman houses.
annotation.definitionFit: Atria were the central open courts of ancient Roman houses.

clue.text: Bad season for children (9)

annotation.surface: It's been a poor time of year for kids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad' means gone off, as spoiled food is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: offspring are the young a parent produces, so children in the human case.

clue.text: Girl primarily broadcasting false information (3)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: Fi is a girl's name, short for Fiona

annotation.surface: A girl is mainly spreading misinformation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' looks as if it applies to 'Girl', giving G; it applies to 'broadcasting', and the girl is FI in full.
annotation.definitionFit: A fib is a trivial lie, a bit of false information.

clue.text: Senior citizen squaddie perhaps shaved? (5)

indicators.note: SOLDIER has its edges shaved off, losing first and last letters

blocks.note: a squaddie is a private soldier, British slang
SOLDIER with its outer letters S and R shaved off

annotation.surface: An old soldier, maybe with an army haircut.
annotation.walkthrough: A squaddie is British slang for a private soldier; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a soldier. 'Shaved' suits a recruit's haircut.
annotation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an old person, a senior citizen.

clue.text: Junior officer’s regular payment to change name (9)

blocks.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular payment

annotation.surface: A junior officer's pay is set to be changed by name.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than showing possession. A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain.
annotation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain.
